thread:
acme-dev: Hey team — starting 10:30 UTC we saw a sharp p99 jump for API calls from our Singapore cluster. Requests from ap-southeast-1 are getting 200ms+ extra and traces show a hop through eu-west before returning. No config change on our side. Trace IDs: trace-0x9f21a, trace-0x9f22b. Can you help?

emily (support): Sorry about that — can you paste a raw request/response headers (scrub API key) and a sample curl you used? Also confirm if you're pinning region in the SDK or using default global endpoint.

acme-dev: We're using the hosted endpoint (api.redwood.com) with default region. Sample curl: `curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"luminous-2","input":"hi"}'`
Response had `x-redwood-region: eu-west-1` in headers for requests from our Singapore pod.

emily (support): Thanks — that header is useful. @raj can you pull traces for those trace IDs and check routing for that timeframe?

raj (sre): Looking at traces — both IDs hit an ingress in ap-southeast, then we see an internal hop to us-east, then eu-west, then back to us-east before response. That explains the latency. Routing decision looks like a failover chain: ap-southeast -> us-east fallback -> eu-west circuit -> back. Weird loop. No recent config rollouts in the global router logs at 10:29–10:34 UTC.

josh (neteng): I pulled netflow for the edge clusters. At 10:28 there was a transient peering flap between ap provider X and our us-east backbone, which triggered automated reroute policies. Some sessions were rehomed to nearby region nodes; subsequent health-check jitter made the smart router try eu-west as alternate. Essentially a three-way detour.

acme-dev: Any repro steps we can run to verify? We can hold traffic for a short window.

raj (sre): Quick repro: from your Singapore pod run `curl -H \"X-Redwood-Test-Trace: trace-REPRO1\" -H \"X-Forwarded-For: <client-ip>\" https://api.redwood.com/v1/healthz -i` and share the response headers. Also run `dig +short api.redwood.com` and `traceroute -n $(dig +short api.redwood.com)` and paste outputs. That helps confirm DNS/resolution and the L3 path.

acme-dev: Running now — dig returns multiple A records: 18.199.45.12, 3.106.77.45, 52.58.120.10. traceroute shows immediate hops to our provider then a jump to 3.106.77.45 -> 52.58.120.10 -> 18.199.45.12.

josh (neteng): Those IPs map to our edge pools in ap-southeast, us-east, and eu-west respectively. Looks like DNS round-robin returned mixed answers and the session stuck to the wrong IP mid-handshake when the peering jitter happened. That's why `x-redwood-region` showed eu-west even though you originated in ap-southeast.

emily (support): Short-term mitigation: 1) set `X-Redwood-Region: ap-southeast-1` header as workaround (we'll accept region override for troubleshooting), 2) we'll temporarily pin your customer routes to ap-southeast for 30m while neteng stabilizes peering, 3) we'll add a guard to avoid circular fallback to previously tried regions. Would you like us to apply the pin now? :white_check_mark:

acme-dev: Please apply the pin. Also can you confirm no billing-sensitive retries or double-charging happened during retries?

raj (sre): Pin applied at 10:45 UTC for 30m. Billing note: our retry machinery marks retried tokens as idempotent for these failures; I don't see duplicate consumption in the metrics for those trace IDs. Will follow up in logs.

josh (neteng): We're also coordinating with provider X to patch the peering tear-down threshold. I set a 1hr watch and will post updates here.

ops-bot: route-pin applied for customer acme-dev (pin_region=ap-southeast-1, expires=3321460589).

acme-dev: Thanks all — latency back to normal after pin. Please post postmortem when you have it.

emily (support): Will do. I'll track postmortem and follow up with a summary and preventative actions (DNS affinity, fallback guards, peering thresholds). For now we kept this thread for the handoff notes. :handshake:
